answer: Copper-latency registration gate. New agent identities must submit their first three transactions with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a hidden schedule, and nodes reject identities whose gaps fall below a per-epoch floor. An attacker must hold each fake identity open across several epochs to shape traffic plausibly, not fire it in one burst. The island of legitimate agents absorbs this delay cheaply because real work already spans time; a sybil farm pays wall-clock latency and idle connection cost per identity.
